claims.text: Choice architecture can be used to nudge individuals into making better decisions than they would otherwise make.
Issues related to meaning can pose methodological problems for designing effective choice architecture.

evidence.description: Thaler and Sunstein's Nudge presents an influential account of why choice architecture should be used to nudge people into making better decisions.
The essay clarifies why issues related to meaning can pose methodological problems for creating effective choice architecture.

limitations.text: Practical difficulties and conceptual problems arise during nudge practice.
Nudging faces ethical and political objections regarding its implementation and philosophy.
Issues related to meaning pose methodological problems for creating effective choice architecture.
